reviewed_surface: Package mutations under HOMEBREW_PREFIX (default /opt/homebrew), unresolved downloads and package scripts; service start/stop; explicit inert queries; unknown subcommands stay bounded.

bunx aliases the npx package runner, with a bare --bun flag and nested command argv preserved; each runner's own options end at the command. npx alone has -c/--call, which runs its value as a shell body only when no operand follows, after installing any --package packages.
POSIX unlink(1) removes each named entry with the unlink system call; it takes no recursion or force switch, and --help/--version only report.

rimraf 4 and later recursively delete each operand, without prompting unless -i; --glob/-g makes operands glob patterns and --no-glob/-G keeps them literal; -h only reports. rimraf 3 and earlier expand globs by default, so the default form discloses that version dependence.

Content filters that read each file operand (or standard input) and write its contents, reformatted, to standard output: tac, fold, fmt, expand, paste, column and shuf from coreutils/util-linux, and hexdump/hd. The declared options are those GNU/util-linux and BSD agree on; where they differ an option is left undeclared (fmt -p takes a value only in GNU, so only --prefix is declared) or over-reports reads (BSD fmt -t takes a number). shuf -e and -i read no file. Obsolete numeric options, hexdump -f/-L, shuf -o/--random-source and every undeclared option stay unrecognized.
